analysis: Examined the supplied changes: documentation in docs/developer/test.md (head lines 1849-2513, plus the 2026-10-31 date bump and the CI shard-lane notes shown in the file_changes excerpt) and the CI routing test script scripts/test-darkbloom-route.py (patch hunks). The doc text describes test procedures for cluster, TP, GPT-OSS, MiMo, Gemma and Qwen native checks, including the prefix tenant partition table and SSD prefix record encoding checks. It changes no runtime code, protocol, key custody, attestation, or cache behavior. The prefix-cache tenant-partition and SSD-record test descriptions are consistent with the existing T-041 posture: account-scoped salt, HMAC lookup, and TTL are unchanged. They state that real-model tenant isolation remains a hardware gate, so they claim nothing beyond the threat model. The routing test script change makes each test-provider shard read its own lane, `test-provider-<shard>`, via the new SHARDED set and helpers matrix_shards, job_lanes and requested_lanes. It only asserts workflow structure: runs-on expressions, the per-lane fallback labels, and the count and permission checks. It grants no new permissions, the route job is still checked for permissions {} and no secrets, and release and credentialed workflows are still asserted to keep literal runners. The workflow YAML itself (ci.yml) and the darkbloom-route.yml router and plane are not in the supplied evidence. So I could not verify that the real workflow matches these test expectations, or how the plane handles per-shard lanes. That is a CI availability and routing-integrity question, not a demonstrated regression, and it is outside the provider/native threat model scope. The second patch excerpt is truncated, so some test-script hunks could not be reviewed. No security regressions or threat-model gaps were identified in the visible content.
